title: "Which muscles, and when: space-by-time muscle synergies"
subtitle: "A worked sNM3F case study on real forearm EMG"
categories: [emg, muscle-synergy, dimensionality-reduction, validated]
author: "Yusuke Matsui"
date: "2026-08-17"

> **What this case shows** — spatial NMF answers *which* muscles group together;
> **space-by-time** (sNM3F) also answers *when*. On real 16-channel forearm EMG,
> it factorises each trial's **960-value** muscle × time envelope into a few
> **shared spatial modules** and **shared temporal modules** plus a tiny per-trial
> **activation matrix**: a **2×2 model** (4 shared modules) reconstructs the
> 14-trial EMG at **VAF 0.958**, a 3×3 model at **0.968** — so each trial is
> compressed to a handful of activation numbers over common modules, and those
> activations carry the gesture **above chance** (leave-one-out **0.64** vs 0.50).
> **How to read it** — left, the spatial modules (which channels co-activate);
> centre, the temporal modules (when); right, VAF rising with model size.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — decompose a *set* of muscle × time EMG trials into **shared
spatial** synergies (muscle groupings), **shared temporal** synergies (activation
timing) and a **per-trial activation** matrix that combines them.
**Way of thinking** — "which muscles" and "when" are *separable* questions:
space-by-time keeps the modules common across trials and puts the task-to-task
difference where it belongs — in the small activation matrix — turning each trial
into a few interpretable numbers.
**Ecosystem usage** — `spaceByTimeSynergy()` (PhysioEMG); compare with
`muscleSynergy()` (spatial only), `muscleSynergyTensor()` (PARAFAC) and
`tuckerSynergy()` (non-diagonal core).
:::

## Proposition

Space-by-time factorises multi-trial EMG into shared spatial + temporal modules
with a per-trial activation. On real forearm EMG a compact model reconstructs at
high VAF (2×2 = 0.958), VAF rises monotonically with modules, and the activations
carry the gesture above chance (LOO 0.64).

## Question & goal

**The question separates structure from task.** A muscle × time EMG matrix mixes
two things: a fixed *coordination structure* (which muscles fire together, in what
temporal sequence) and a *task-specific drive* (how strongly each is recruited this
trial). Space-by-time pulls them apart. We ask whether, on real forearm EMG, it
compresses the signal into shared modules at high fidelity and leaves the task in
the activations.

## Challenge & approach

We take 16-channel forearm EMG envelopes for two gestures × seven trials,
time-normalise each to 60 points, and run `spaceByTimeSynergy()` for 1–4 modules.
We read the reconstruction VAF, confirm it rises with model size, and test whether
a nearest-centroid classifier on the per-trial **activations** recovers the gesture
(leave-one-out).

## Data

**GRABMyo** (Pradhan et al., PhysioNet) — 16 forearm EMG channels, two gestures ×
seven trials, enveloped and normalised. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![The shared spatial modules (left, which channels co-activate), the shared
temporal modules (centre, when), and reconstruction VAF versus model size
(right).](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left heatmap and centre curves are **shared by every
trial** — the coordination structure. Only the small activation matrix changes
trial to trial, yet 4 modules already reconstruct the EMG at 96%.

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| VAF, 1×1 module | 0.930 |
| VAF, 2×2 modules | **0.958** |
| VAF, 3×3 modules | 0.968 |
| gesture LOO accuracy (from activations) | **0.64** (chance 0.50) |
| trials decomposed | 14 |

## Conclusion

Space-by-time compresses real multi-trial EMG into a few shared spatial and
temporal modules at high fidelity, with the task living in a tiny activation
matrix. The transferable takeaway: **factor "which muscles" and "when" separately —
the shared modules are the coordination structure, and the per-trial activations
are the compact, task-carrying code.**

## Open questions

- With **more gestures and participants** the activations should separate tasks far
  more sharply (a decoding case in its own right), and the shared modules could be
  tested for cross-participant invariance. Here, two similar gestures give only a
  *modest* 0.64 activation accuracy. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| step | function | package |
|---|---|---|
| envelope + normalise each channel | `emgEnvelope()` / `emgAmplitudeNormalize()` | PhysioEMG |
| space-by-time (spatial × temporal + activations) | `spaceByTimeSynergy()` | PhysioEMG |
| spatial-only synergies | `muscleSynergy()` | PhysioEMG |
| hierarchical (non-diagonal core) | `tuckerSynergy()` | PhysioEMG |

**Choosing the parameters:** give one non-negative `muscle × time` matrix per
trial (same time length), pick the spatial and temporal module counts from the VAF
curve (the knee), and read the per-trial **activations** as the compact task code.

```r
library(PhysioEMG)
fit <- spaceByTimeSynergy(trials, n_spatial = 2, n_temporal = 2)
fit$vaf; fit$spatial; fit$temporal; fit$activation[[1]]
```

One line for the technical reader: every number traces to
[`artifacts/spacetime_summary.csv`](artifacts/spacetime_summary.csv) and
[`artifacts/vaf_curve.csv`](artifacts/vaf_curve.csv), re-checked by
[`audit.py`](audit.py) and `tools/validate_case.py`.
